question: Partway through a long agentic session, a developer changes several aspects of the next request while keeping the tools array and system prompt text identical to the previous call. Which of the following changes will invalidate the cached message-level content for that next request? (Select all that apply.)
options: A) Adding a cache_control breakpoint on a block that lacked one before
B) Requesting a different max_tokens value for the assistant's next reply
C) Switching the thinking parameter's budget for the upcoming turn
D) Changing the tool_choice setting from "auto" to a specific named tool
E) Attaching a new image to the most recent user message in the conversation
F) Appending a new user message onto the end without changing earlier turns
correct_answers: C) Switching the thinking parameter's budget for the upcoming turn
D) Changing the tool_choice setting from "auto" to a specific named tool
E) Attaching a new image to the most recent user message in the conversation
explanations: Incorrect. Adding a new breakpoint establishes an additional cache entry; it does not invalidate existing cached content.
Incorrect. max_tokens controls the length of the generated reply and is not one of the factors that invalidates cached prompt content.
Correct. Changing thinking parameters invalidates the message-level cache.
Correct. Changing tool_choice invalidates the message-level cache.
Correct. Adding an image to a message is one of the changes that invalidates the message-level cache.
Incorrect. Appending a new message without altering earlier turns is the normal, expected way conversations grow under caching; it does not invalidate the cache for the unchanged earlier content.
